findings.title: Commission read APIs have no permission check
findings.what: GET /v1/commission-plans, /commission-plans/:id, /commission-calculations(/:id), /commission-payables answer any signed-in user of the tenant. The sidebar hides Commission unless the user holds finance.view, commission.plan.edit or commission.plan.approve.
findings.evidence: finance/finance-service.ts:195 listCommissionPlans reads by tenant with no assertPermission, while updateCommissionPlan (line 211) does assert; real-database probe as a zero-permission user: 200 on all three lists, 404 (lookup first) on the by-id routes.
findings.fix: Add assertPermission(ctx, "finance.view") (or a dedicated commission.read) to the read methods; add 403 tests for a zero-grant user and a sales role.

findings.title: Sanction and disbursement read APIs have no permission check
findings.what: GET /v1/sanctions, /sanctions/:id, /sanctions/:id/tranches, /tranches/:id, /disbursements and /lender-cases/:id/sanctions answer any signed-in user. The sidebar shows Sanction and disbursement only to sanction.record, disbursement.record or disbursement.verify holders.
findings.evidence: origination/sanctions/repository.ts:113 listAllSanctions filters by tenant only; real-database probe: 200 on /sanctions and /disbursements, 404 on by-id routes (lookup before any check).
findings.fix: Require the sanction/disbursement read permission used by the screen (or application.read for the case-scoped list) in the service; add zero-grant and sales-role tests.

findings.title: Manual ledger journal posting has no permission check, and the ledger audit actions are invalid
findings.what: POST /v1/ledger/journals has no authorization (the read GET /v1/ledger/journals needs finance.view). Separately, the audit actions ledger.journal.post, ledger.period.close and ledger.export.run have two dots and violate the audit_event CHECK (action ~ ^[a-z_]+\.[a-z_]+$), so those three operations fail on a database built from the migrations.
findings.evidence: ledger/ledger-service.ts:122 postJournal goes straight to the period check; probe on a throwaway database: a zero-permission user reached the audit insert and was stopped by audit_event_action_check (422, nothing committed). Severity becomes CRITICAL the moment the audit action is fixed without adding the check.
findings.fix: Add a finance posting permission check to postJournal; rename the three audit actions to the allowed shape (for example ledger.journal_posted); add tests for both.

findings.title: Any signed-in user can write forged security events
findings.what: POST /v1/security/events records an event with caller-chosen type, principal, IP and severity. The list endpoints need security.incident.
findings.evidence: security/service.ts:81 recordSecurityEvent has no check; probe on a throwaway database: zero-permission user got 201 and a security_event row was written.
findings.fix: Restrict the endpoint to a service identity or security.incident; derive principal and IP from the request instead of the body.

findings.title: Decision evaluation endpoint has no authorization found
findings.what: POST /v1/decisions/:decisionKey/evaluations calls the decision engine without a permission check in the router or the engine; simulation routes in the same file require rule.simulate.
findings.evidence: rules/api/router.ts:673 and rules/engine/decision-engine.ts:30 (decide). Static trace only: not exercised with a valid payload.
findings.fix: Confirm the intended callers; require rule.simulate (or a service identity) and test.

findings.title: Import batch list has no permission check
findings.what: GET /v1/imports lists every import batch of the tenant to any signed-in user, while report download and commit are gated by requireTargetPermission.
findings.evidence: platform/imports/service.ts:452 listBatches; probe: 200 for a zero-permission user.
findings.fix: Apply the same import.run / config.manage / target-create check to the list and detail reads.

findings.title: Home page offers 18 module cards to every customer-tenant user
findings.what: The cards (Leads, Decision Rules, User Management, Access Control, Commissions, Payouts, Tenant Configuration and others) are filtered only by realm, not by permission. A Sales Executive sees links that lead to refusals or, for Commissions and Sanctions, to open data.
findings.evidence: web shell/HomePage.tsx:7-111 (cards) and :121 (filter).
findings.fix: Filter cards with the same anyOf rules as the sidebar (reuse NAV_GROUPS).

findings.title: No route-level permission guard anywhere in the web app
findings.what: AppLayout checks the session and MFA only. A user who types /commission, /roles or /payouts gets the page shell and then API errors; 52 of 76 feature files contain no permission check at all.
findings.evidence: web shell/AppLayout.tsx:60,89; routes.tsx:34-40; fe inventory (52/76).
findings.fix: Add a route wrapper that takes the matching anyOf from NAV_GROUPS and renders a "not permitted" page.

findings.title: Qloax tenant admin role holds the six platform operator permissions
findings.what: ROLE-TENANT-ADMIN of qloax-dsa holds platform.console, flags, jobs, master_data, release and support_access, as demo-alpha does. The platform realm refuses tenant users and the menu is hidden, but the grants should not exist (Module 1 check 16).
findings.evidence: read-only hosted query of app.role_permission on 2026-10-19: demo-alpha and qloax-dsa each have the six; no other customer tenant has any.
findings.fix: Same prepared removal as demo-alpha (tools/sql/fixes), after approval; make the provisioning script stop copying them.

findings.title: Nine permissions are defined but granted to no role
findings.what: commission.calculate, commission.plan.edit, commission.plan.approve, customer.reveal_sensitive, lead.reopen, lender.read, lender.manage, product.read, product.manage. Features that need them cannot be used by any role: commission plan edit/approval, revealing sensitive customer data, reopening a lead.
findings.evidence: hosted catalogue and role_permission (99 permissions); migration 0060 defines them and grants none; docs/PERMISSION_RECONCILIATION.md.
findings.fix: Business decision on which roles hold each; then a grant migration (needs approval).

findings.title: Staff email and workload visible to every signed-in user
findings.what: GET /v1/workforce/agents returns displayName, email, availability, capacity and live lead/application counts to any signed-in user. Workforce has no permission rule in the sidebar by design.
findings.evidence: probe on a throwaway database: fields id, displayName, email, primaryBranchId, availability, capacity, activeLeadCount, activeApplicationCount.
findings.fix: Decide whether all staff should see this; if not, require workforce.read or restrict to managers.

findings.title: Lead action buttons ignore permissions
findings.what: Qualify, Disqualify, Convert and Assign appear by lead state only. A user with lead.read but without lead.qualify, lead.assign or application.create sees them and gets a refusal.
findings.evidence: web features/leads/LeadDetail.tsx:192-255 (no permission test); API checks per action (lead-service.ts:232,518,814,957).
findings.fix: Hide or disable each button with the permission its endpoint requires.

findings.title: Access control menu omits role.manage
findings.what: The sidebar item needs user.manage; the API accepts user.manage or role.manage. ROLE-ORG-OWNER holds role.manage but not user.manage and cannot see the screen.
findings.evidence: web shell/Sidebar.tsx (Access control anyOf) versus sweep: GET /v1/roles opens with user.manage | role.manage.
findings.fix: Use anyOf [user.manage, role.manage] (the dead navigation.ts already does).

findings.title: Dead duplicate navigation config
findings.what: shell/navigation.ts defines a second, different set of visibility rules that nothing in the app imports (only its spec does).
findings.evidence: grep: imported only by navigation.spec.ts.
findings.fix: Delete it and its spec or make it the single source for sidebar, Home and route guards.

findings.title: Duplicate sidebar entry
findings.what: "Performance Dashboard" (Team and performance) and "Performance Dashboards" (Reporting) both link to /performance.
findings.evidence: web shell/Sidebar.tsx.
findings.fix: Remove one.

findings.title: Tenant directory reads are open to every signed-in user
findings.what: GET /v1/users (id, display name, branch, status, availability), /branches, /teams, /work-queues, /delegations and /tenant answer any signed-in user. Needed for pickers, but the sidebar lists the matching admin screens as admin-only.
findings.evidence: probe on a throwaway database.
findings.fix: Decision: keep reads open and say so, or require config.manage/user.manage for the admin screens' data.

findings.title: Same role code, different grants in different tenants
findings.what: ROLE-COMPLIANCE lacks audit.read, customer.read, lead.read, application.read, audit.export_evidence in demo-dsa and the three test tenants; ROLE-RM in demo-dsa lacks application.* and lead.qualify; BRANCH-MGR and RM in demo-beta lack customer.create/update.
findings.evidence: hosted role_permission comparison against qloax-dsa.
findings.fix: Align or document; test tenants are fixtures.

findings.title: Catalogue mismatches
findings.what: finance.period_close exists in the contracts but not in the hosted catalogue; eligibility.override is listed twice in PERMISSION_CODES; security.vuln is granted but never used by API or web.
findings.evidence: packages/contracts/src/permissions.ts; hosted app.permission.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate; decide on finance.period_close and security.vuln.

findings.title: Role navigation tests cover 9 of 14 roles
findings.what: shell/role-navigation.spec.ts covers Commission Approver, Compliance, Doc Verifier, Finance Exec, Loan Ops, RM, Rule Approver, Rule Author, Sales Exec. Missing: Org Owner, Tenant Admin, Branch Manager, Team Manager, Verifier.
findings.evidence: file read.
findings.fix: Add the five roles using the live grant sets.

findings.title: Deferred endpoints answer 409 to everyone
findings.what: POST /v1/tasks/:id/snooze, /tasks/bulk-reassignment and PUT /v1/customers/:id/preferences always throw INVALID_STATE (deferred to later releases).
findings.evidence: crm/tasks/router.ts:208,216; crm/customers/router.ts:208.
findings.fix: None until built; add the permission check when implemented.

findings.title: Lender and product catalogue reads are open; their permissions are unused
findings.what: GET /v1/lenders and /v1/products (and sub-resources) have no check; lender.read/lender.manage/product.read/product.manage exist, are granted to no role and are not referenced by the API.
findings.evidence: probe: 200 for zero-permission user; permission reconciliation.
findings.fix: Decision: keep catalogue read open to all staff (and drop the unused codes) or wire the codes and grant them.

findings.title: Platform routes are correctly realm-gated
findings.what: All 19 /platform/v1 routes refused a tenant user with every permission (the new tenant flag routes included).
findings.evidence: permission sweep and platform tests.
findings.fix: None.

sidebar.label: Teams

sidebar.label: Work queues

sidebar.label: Access control

sidebar.label: Import and export
sidebar.note: UI needs import.run|export.run; GET /v1/imports has no permission check (F-06).
